# Arkpedia stage simulator

Public GPL-3.0-or-later fork of [Stronghold Protocol](https://github.com/sganggs/Stronghold-Protocol), initially based on `19a89085a4c9a773a7b88437d7cd79c3e7131cfd`. Preserve LICENSE, NOTICE.md, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, the Spine linking permission and upstream contributor credit. The private Arkpedia app embeds this separately served application; it contains no copied private application code or account data.

## Run the playable MVP

```sh
npm ci
npm run start:arkpedia
# http://localhost:3182/arkpedia/
npm run test:arkpedia
```

The maintainer workflow for adding an enemy, a stage or an operator is in
[docs/ADDING-CONTENT.md](docs/ADDING-CONTENT.md).

This entry needs no upstream release archive or full game-art download. `npm ci` copies the bundled Three.js, Pixi and Spine browser dependencies. The browser downloads 0-1's original stage art, the chosen squad's Front/Back models and this stage's enemies from a pinned `arkpedia-sd-assets` commit. The inherited `npm start` still opens the original Stronghold application.

Full source-identity tests read original skeleton bytes from the sibling SD directory. `node tools/arkpedia/test-assets.mjs` prepares every snapshot-referenced skeleton from its immutable SD commit and verifies its size/hash, including existing files; changed files fail rather than being overwritten. This small test dependency is separate from full texture/scenery/browser validation. CI runs the preparation before the complete suite and allows 90 minutes per Linux/Windows and Node 22/24 matrix entry. Snapshot replacement retries bounded transient Windows rename locks while preserving atomic visibility; it never deletes the old target to work around a lock.

For loopback development, `start:arkpedia` uses the sibling asset repository by default. It serves only immutable Git blobs from the snapshot's full commit, under `/arkpedia-assets/<commit>/`; untracked/modified files and arbitrary refs cannot replace battle art. Source hashes still apply. A missing sibling checkout falls back to the pinned published URLs. Hosted/non-loopback runs keep those published URLs. Asset commits must be published before changing the simulator pin.

To embed it in Arkpedia's overhaul branch, run the private application with `NEXT_PUBLIC_STAGE_SIMULATOR_URL=http://localhost:3182/arkpedia/`, then visit `/stages/simulator`. The iframe is loaded only after opening its fullscreen workspace. Its prototype link appears only on 0-1 when that URL is configured. No production simulator host has been configured.

## Original stage assets

0-1 uses the actual scene from the official Global Android resource version `26-09-23-17-49-43_b9cc4a`, published in `arkpedia-sd-assets`. Its 177 static submeshes, original colour/emission textures, baked lightmap and source tile heights are about 1.7 MB combined. The scene's gameplay-geometry hash and every file's SHA-256 must match before it replaces the simplified map. Missing or mismatched art leaves an explicitly labelled fallback. Rendering approximates the Unity shader; lighting is not yet a frame-for-frame match.

The pinned 0-1 lightmap is ETC2 RGBA with Unity RGBM encoding. The browser linearizes its RGB through sRGB texture sampling, then decodes the alpha multiplier using the [Unity RGBM range and exponent](https://docs.unity3d.com/2021.3/Documentation/Manual/Lightmaps-TechnicalInformation.html). Three's Lambert normalization is compensated for baked diffuse lighting. Ambient fill points along the stage's Z-up axis. This preserves the source light/shadow gradients instead of treating the encoded bake as an ordinary colour image; no asset brightness filter is applied.

The exporter preserves world-space static batches once, reverses Z/triangle winding for the renderer, removes the centered map anchor, and keeps the already-baked lightmap UVs. It does not apply the prefab transforms a second time or reuse an unrelated Stronghold map theme.

Entry and defence markers use the original five standard box meshes and shared atlas from `arts/effects/[pack]map.ab` in that same Global version. The red and blue frames include the original warning/arrow symbols. They sit at source tile heights, are independent of the path overlay, and render above static buildings so entry points remain visible. Actor sprites render in front. Their additive/alpha materials and gentle intensity pulse approximate the game effect; they are not a verified reproduction of Unity's animation curve. The manifest pins and checksums the marker pack separately; a failed load is labelled in the map status.

To reproduce the pack (Python 3.13+, Node 22+):

```sh
python3 -m venv .cache/map-env
.cache/map-env/bin/pip install -r tools/arkpedia/stages/requirements.txt
node tools/arkpedia/stages/fetch-bundles.mjs --version 26-09-23-17-49-43_b9cc4a
.cache/map-env/bin/python tools/arkpedia/stages/export-scene.py --bundles .cache/arkpedia/map-source/ab --manifest .cache/arkpedia/map-source/hot_update_list.json --out .cache/arkpedia/stage-pack --version 26-09-23-17-49-43_b9cc4a --base-url https://ark-us-static-online.yo-star.com/assetbundle/official/Android/assets/26-09-23-17-49-43_b9cc4a
# Standard entry/defence effects are a separate small bundle.
node tools/arkpedia/stages/fetch-bundles.mjs --version 26-09-23-17-49-43_b9cc4a --gates-only
.cache/map-env/bin/python tools/arkpedia/stages/export-gates.py --bundles .cache/arkpedia/map-source/ab --manifest .cache/arkpedia/map-source/hot_update_list.json --out .cache/arkpedia/gate-pack --version 26-09-23-17-49-43_b9cc4a
```

The fetcher verifies unzipped bundle size/MD5 against the game manifest. Publication to the asset repository and updating its immutable simulator pin remain explicit steps; this does not automatically refresh the full stage catalogue. Game assets retain their original ownership (see `arkpedia-sd-assets/NOTICE.md`). The extractor stays in this GPL repository.

## Supported slice

- 0-1 **Collapse**: source terrain, spawn times, both routes (including the soldier's wait), stage-specific soldier DEF, DP regeneration/cap, deployment limit and life points.
- Fang, Melantha, Beagle, Kroos, Hibiscus, Steward, Vanilla, Cardigan, Orchid, Plume, Popukar, Adnachiel, Lava, Catapult, Midnight, Ansel and Spot: selectable E0/E1, level, potential, trust and skill rank; their actual ranges, stats, basic traits, promotion talents and S1s.
- Vanilla grants DP when her manual ATK skill starts; Cardigan immediately heals herself by a percentage of talent-adjusted max HP; Orchid deals Arts damage, slows on hit and gains the source ASPD talent/skill bonuses.
- Plume gains one DP for each enemy she defeats, refunds her original potential-adjusted DP cost on manual retreat (including later deployments), and uses her source ATK/ASPD S1 buff. Death grants no refund.
- Popukar attacks up to her block count of enemies in range, prioritizing those she blocks, and has her source HP/ATK talents and S1 ATK buff. This does not enable splash attacks for single-target guards.
- Adnachiel retains aerial priority at E0 and gains source ASPD/ranged-enemy priority at E1, with his source S1 ATK buff.
- Lava receives her promotion/potential-dependent starting SP on each deployment; her S1 speeds up her normal Arts splash attacks.
- Catapult uses physical splash attacks, her E1 DP discount and source S1 blast-area multiplier; the skill leaves targeting range unchanged. The base splash radius still uses the inherited profession profile pending client-prefab verification.
- Midnight keeps the lord ranged damage penalty when his critical talent triggers; S1 applies the source ATK buff and changes attacks to Arts until expiry.
- Ansel rolls his source extra-heal talent once per heal and selects a distinct injured, healable ally in his current range. His S1 extends healing range and raises ATK.
- Spot switches to healing in the source 3×3 skill range while retaining block capacity. His client prefab adds the skill blackboard attack-time value to base attack time; the heal grants a promotion/potential-dependent, refreshing three-second physical-dodge buff. See `data/arkpedia-spot-prefab.json` for pinned prefab evidence.
- Up to 12 unique squad members plus one distinct maxed support. The current selectable roster has 381 operator forms and 832 source skills; support is limited to that same supported roster. Supported four-, five- and six-stars have every source skill, source E0/E1/E2 caps and rank 1–7/M1/M2/M3 with promotion and level unlocks checked. Changing promotion clamps level and skill rank and selects an unlocked skill. A maxed support retains the chosen skill independently of the squad's builds.
- Drag an operator onto a valid tile and choose its facing on the map; click/keyboard placement, Escape cancellation, surface-only deployment feedback and a continuous attack-range outline; blocking, physical/Arts attacks, healing, time/attack SP, manual/automatic skills, manual retreat/refund, increasing deployment costs, redeployment cooldown, clear/defeat.
- Original 0-1 Chernobog meshes, textures, scenery and baked lighting, original red entry/blue defence boxes, rendered with Three.js and animated Spine chibis; optional existing-viewer path overlay; pause, 1×/2×, restart, fullscreen/mobile viewport workspace, pause on native-fullscreen exit or hidden tab.

The battle UI uses in-game-style overlays on a full-height battlefield: centered enemy/life counters, speed/pause at the upper right, a settings menu at the upper left, and DP/remaining slots above the bottom portrait shelf. Paths, restart and squad exit live in settings. The shelf uses pinned original portraits, class icons, DP costs and rarity edges, with a visible scroll track and direct arrows. Selecting an operator opens a fixed left artwork/stats panel with independently scrolling Skill/Trait/Talent content. Original trait descriptions are additive display metadata from the same pinned Global datamine; existing combat records are unchanged.

Dragging onto a legal tile highlights deployment surfaces in green. Dropping opens a white diamond centered on that tile and a separate red Cancel control; deployment still waits for a new centre-to-direction swipe and release. Returning into the dead zone preserves pending placement and spends no DP. The attack range uses clipped orange stripes on the actual tile surfaces. Keyboard direction selection and Enter remain supported; edge controls stay inside the battlefield without moving the handle away from its operator. Deployed units have tile-anchored retreat and skill controls, live SP readouts and green ready feedback, using the same skill runtime as the HP/SP gauges. Landscape phone layouts keep the same structure and retain the rotation gate. This interface is independently implemented here, without importing private application code.

Counter widths are reserved. DP recovery follows the actual combat resource and freezes with the battle; spending, refunds and the DP cap update the same readout. Pointer-transparent HUD layers preserve map interaction.

Source-timed unfired attacks and interruptible casts retain accepted control applications, including effects shorter than a combat tick. Recovery before the release frame cannot revive a cancelled hit. Emitted projectiles, persistent fields and explicitly uninterruptible source casts retain their separate lifetimes. Inspire chooses the highest final ATK/DEF/MAX_HP addition per attribute; Vigor and Weightless keep the strongest named effect with owned expiry fallback. These tested combat rules do not claim recorded-client frame parity.

Map tags come from the pinned original level file, with a source path and SHA-256; chapter talents never infer tags from a stage name.

Summon cards use original token stats and artwork. Deepcolor spends five DP, a deployment slot and stock per Tentacle; direct drops select the deployed token. Roberta's Modelers need a facing selection and use no deployment slot; their defence/shield grants follow the original recipient selector. Beanstalk's primary Metal Crab remains on its chosen tile through its rest/rebirth cycle; its retreat control triggers that cycle and skill-created extra crabs have their own expiry. Summoner withdrawal cleans up owned units. Beeswax creates her original Obelisk automatically on a source-eligible tile when S2 resolves, with source blocking, burst, no-heal/no-regeneration and owned lifetime rules. Shamare's S2 supplies a five-DP doll card with one stock, no deployment slot, fixed facing, source skill-rank debuffs and a 15-second lifetime. Nightingale's E2 adds two original Cage cards on each deployment while retaining unused stock. Cages use no deployment slot, no facing choice or attacks, cannot be healed, have physical dodge and lose 3% Max HP per second after the first one-second delay. Their source stats, three-unit limit, shared cooldown and owner cleanup are tested. Silence S2 replenishes one original Healing Drone card and pauses SP when stock is full. The drone costs five DP, occupies no deployment slot, needs no facing choice, heals eligible surrounding allies continuously and withdraws after ten seconds. Original passive drone art is used without inventing attack events. Phantom E1 unlocks his original clone card. It costs source token DP and one deployment slot, copies the selected skill/rank, and uses its own original token keyframes rather than owner trust or potential bonuses. Stock/cooldown persists across owner redeploys; E2 reduces the removal-based cooldown. Original distinct Front/Back clone art is imported. Silence the Paradigmatic S2 supplies one zero-DP Night Banisher (Support Drone) only while the selected skill is active. It consumes no deployment slot, has no attacks or HP gauge, and uses its native Start/Idle/Die clips. Removing it starts the selected five-second stock recharge; ending the parent skill withdraws the drone and clears stock. Automatic W mines, Dusk Freelings and Beeswax Obelisks preload their original models with their selected owners, without adding manual deployment cards. Nearl the Radiant Knight S3 preloads its original Blazing Sun, creates it on a source-eligible adjacent free tile, and cleans it up when the parent skill or operator ends. The Sun has no attacks or deployment slot and uses the native static Idle, Start and End clips. Kal’tsit supplies one original Mon3tr card with source DP, one deployment slot, a facing picker and its own level keyframes. Its removal starts the source promotion-based cooldown and restores one stock. Kal’tsit alone can heal her own Mon3tr; independent no-heal and isolation rules still apply. Selecting Mon3tr displays its owner’s SP gauge and bound skill controls while preserving a separate token combat runtime. Owner removal withdraws the summon without its genuine-death burst. Original Attack, Skill, Skill_2, Start, Idle and Die clips are retained. These are explicit adapters, not a generic approval of all summons.

Eyjafjalla, Lin and Goldenglow still need native event/controller verification. Fuze and Coldshot retain original evidence but remain unavailable pending their documented pellet and reload contracts. Ebenholz now has a separately reviewed adapter; his earlier charged-remnant hold remains historical evidence and the unrecovered compiled contracts are explicitly bounded below. Ho'olheyak's earlier distance-curve hold remains historical evidence; her separately reviewed adapter and unresolved final travel distance are documented below. Brigid's earlier bounce/return hold remains historical evidence; her separately reviewed adapter is documented below. Ascalon's earlier hold remains historical evidence; her separately reviewed adapter is documented below. Senshi and Marcille now have separately reviewed regular-stage adapters; their original source holds remain historical evidence. Fang the Fire-Sharpened, Firewatch, Surfer, Melanite and Ash now have separately reviewed adapters; their earlier source holds remain as historical evidence. Native card-cost ordering, bomb startup, DEF-steal lifecycle, piercing falloff and composite/wall dispatch limits are recorded in each enabled adapter's evidence. Wanqing's first-heal timing, Cantabile's native ammo-count event and Erato's active-Sleep ordering are explicit simulator interpretations, not recovered frame parity. New card modifiers operate on this engine's ordinary deployment/redeployment cost; exact native C# rounding/order remains unverified. Original prefab evidence records selectors, per-facing hit events, formula modes and cancellation boundaries. In-game frame comparison and Unity particle/projectile effects remain separate work.

Ch’en now has two-hit normal attacks, all three skills, Scolding's recipient-owned attack/defensive-SP gifts and selected Blade Art bonuses. S1 replaces the two-hit attack with one strike and Stun; S2 separately mitigates Arts/Physical damage within its source cap; S3 uses ten literal-event slashes, nearest substitute selection, final-hit Stun, temporary invulnerability/nonblocking and Stun/Freeze protection. Its eleven-event skeleton versus ten-slash table, numeric cast-state inference, retarget dispatch and native extra-damage ordering remain explicit limits in `data/arkpedia-chen-prefabs.json`. The older Qiubai/Ch’en evidence and deferral are preserved for audit history; this separate adapter records the newer investigation.

Eunectes supports all three source skills and both promotion/potential talents. Her trait stops natural and unforced gift SP while she has no living blockee; initial SP remains available and E2 Resilience increases natural recovery while blocking. S1 is passive ATK/DEF. S2 increases ATK and attack interval, stuns only her current blocked enemies and removes only its own stun on unblock, skill end or withdrawal. S3 grants source ATK/DEF, three Block and continuous healing, uses the original Front mecha clips and ends with five seconds of Stun. Peerless Bravery samples the source half-HP condition every .1 seconds, switching between pre-mitigation damage scaling and nonstacking Sanctuary. `data/arkpedia-eunectes-prefabs.json` retains all 30 ranks, five original bundles, 43 native components, seven templates and both actual facing chains. The eventless transformation uses a bounded 1.5-second Begin followed by the selected skill duration; its native continuation, duration origin, early-stat ownership and interruption timing remain simulator interpretations. Modules, original particles/audio and game-frame parity are not claimed.

Saga supports all three source skills and both promotion/potential talents. Her own ordinary damage leaves enemies at 1 HP; Critical Wounds disable attacks, blocking and healing, slow movement, expire after ten seconds and grant SP to the actual eligible killer. Target-owned wounds survive Saga's withdrawal. S2 stores source charges, grants 4 DP even in an empty cast, strikes up to six current ground enemies in the cross range and eliminates still-wounded victims after the native .7-second delay. S3 uses a current-Block target cap, adds separate Physical damage strictly below half HP and grants one DP on each of its 20 one-second pulses. Clear Mind provides source Physical dodge and continuous healing once per deployment. `data/arkpedia-saga-prefabs.json` retains all 30 ranks, five original bundles, 39 native components, nine templates and both actual facing chains. Shared damage now supports a receipt-only post-shield HP floor without protecting unrelated hits or HP loss. Native controller precedence, event2 DP dispatch, pre-primary extra-hit ordering, threshold equality and tick phases remain explicit simulator interpretations; modules, original particles/audio and game-frame parity are not claimed.

Vulpisfoglia now has all three source skills and both selected talents. Fox Hunt adds independently mitigated Arts damage, including the first receipt, within one nonrefreshing source-owned window per victim. S1 stores three charges and adds NORMAL Arts to its Physical strike; S2 stores two charges, grants DP even in an empty cast, hits up to six ground/air targets and stuns only previously Sluggish enemies. S3 grants DP, extends range, uses a current-Block-attribute target cap, samples decaying ASPD before attacks and earns camouflage on kills; the original half-second checks remove camouflage while blocking and restore it afterward until the next activation. Accelerando changes both natural DP recovery and the HUD while deployed, plus continuous healing after the selected quiet interval. All 30 ranks, five original bundles, 41 native components, 16 templates and both actual facing chains are retained in `data/arkpedia-vulpis-prefabs.json`. Native modifier/controller dispatch, damage ordering, animation overlap and frame parity remain explicit limits; modules and original particles/audio remain separate work.

The source evidence retains unresolved native selector dispatch, animation scaling and effect limitations. Every enabled operator reports `gameFidelityVerified: false`; numerical and scenario tests are not an in-game frame comparison. Corroserum S2 exposes **Stop skill** only while its source-cancellable skill is active; ordinary skills cannot be cancelled that way.

Exusiai's paired BAT interpretation, Thorns' regeneration/counter event phase, Phantom's native random callback order and Snowsant/Almond's hook/link trajectory clocks are explicitly bounded in their prefab evidence. Snowsant S2 maps the source radius0.7 selector to its farthest ground trigger victim; it does not hit the whole attack range. Almond's first-activation SP applies after full cast completion and stays spent across redeploys. These adapters do not claim recovered native C# timing. Archetto retains explicit timing3 per-round selection, saved-input invalidation and post-emission cast/SP limits. Qiubai retains separate initial .5s emission, 4.88s field finish and 5s mode clocks; their native callback phase remains unverified.

Fartooth preserves original range3-9 checks, unmanaged arrows and per-facing attack events, with native selector, mixed-animation and arrow-passive snapshot limits recorded. Saria preserves the literal heal events, selected20s stat-stack timer and fixed S3 pulse fields; legal-overheal SP and native HEAL-purpose filtering remain bounded interpretations. Bagpipe rolls her talent for each separate hit, retains source S2 input/refund and S3 BAT percentage rules, and applies her selected SP bonus from the squad. Her extra-victim selection and native animation/owner-born event ordering are explicitly unverified. Gladiia is implemented with her source link/chant behavior and the fidelity limits recorded below. Aak is implemented with the native dispatch limits recorded below.

Rosa retains born harpoons after owner retirement and releases their owned binds when each original victim is lost; S1/S2 keep normal attacks instead of borrowing S3 clips. Current-ATK link damage, native link-duration overrides and predeck event order are explicitly bounded. Hoederer's source block-based targeting, paid stance flips, independent damage marks and direct HP loss are tested; native eventless startup and damage-receipt phase remain unverified. Puzzle retains typed poison after skill completion/retreat, with independent snapshot, refresh and shared-stack mapping. Its native refresh/trigger-cap law and DP event phase remain explicitly bounded in original prefab evidence.

W's mine selector uses a seeded eligible tile interpretation; owner ATK at mine placement and retained bomb attachment clocks remain explicit source-dispatch limits. Młynar's persistent idle timer, per-family kill handling and Kazimierz damage riders are tested; his original Sanctuary explicitly includes True damage, while ordinary Sanctuary does not. Silence the Paradigmatic retains native HP-bin checks, parent-bound drone stock and two uses of her fatal-protection skill across redeploys. Native callback phases, same-tick aura ordering and repeated-effect selectors remain unverified game-timing boundaries. Her S1 uses Attack, S2 uses Skill and S3 owns its original Skill_2 Begin/Idle/Loop/End forms.

Eyjafjalla the Hvít Aska retains separate HP/elemental recovery and a shared S2 barrier rather than one barrier per recipient. Her S1 and S3 use original forms; periodic callback order, overlapping protection synchronization and five-heal victim selection are bounded mappings. Jieyun retains source high-ground placement, a one-time ATK/cost adjustment, and a chakram that moves to a legal source-range tile, persists after owner withdrawal and checks its per-enemy hit cooldown. Its seeded tile selector and post-withdrawal ATK snapshot are explicit interpretations. Nearl the Radiant Knight S2 alone exempts its owner from the deployment limit. Previous operator history, automatic retreat/refund/redeploy modifiers, eventless birth callbacks, the Sun's adjacent tile selector and host-ATK transfer are documented limits. Nian retains S1 ordinary attack animation and S3’s native Skill_2 family. S2 is disarmed and conservatively uses Idle because its graph requests no recoverable skill clip. Her strongest squad HP contribution, retaliation callback order, status-resistance loader and aura synchronization remain bounded mappings. Kal’tsit retains the .1-second token-validity check, exact token attack events and one-second S3 ATK-decay updates. Native static death-projectile arrival, direct PURE penalty fatal safeguards and owner/token event order are explicit limits. Modules are not enabled by these adapters.

Zuo Le retains first-only attack beginning clips, fixed multi-strike victims after the first release, persistent capped barriers and seven literal S3 attack events. SELF selector phases, accepted-output healing/shield conversion and the full two-second S3 action/SP hold are bounded mappings, with the separate native 1.2-second calculation retained. Bobbing retains five first-hit Burn pulses using current ATK, literal skill beginnings and a stationary perpendicular field. Native parent/subordinate command epochs are bounded: the main skill ends at 11 seconds while the already-born field lasts to 11.5 seconds. Scene uses its original token keyframes and finite 3/4/5 promotion stock, a shared ten-second placement cooldown, independent reveal and conditional camouflage. S2 replenishes stock and boosts owned cameras before issuing the retained remote self-stun command. Remote dispatch order and the controlled-state renderer remain explicit limits; the native Stun clip is retained and no Start clip is invented.

Chilchuck cancels only explicitly marked environmental HP damage or environmental elemental injury; ordinary sourceless damage, gauges, bursts and direct HP loss remain unchanged. His S1 translates the literal three-step conditional Dice graph rather than a uniform DP range. Normal ranged/melee origins, source attack events and S2 accepted output DP are tested. Independent RNG calls, recursive reset/late-enable order, event4 payment at the selected three-second duration and active-at-impact payment remain explicit native-dispatch limits.

Blacknight uses one zero-DP, zero-slot tactical point inside the owner's attack range, with source promotion stats, a one-second beginning/rebirth and separate 20/17/15-second recovery. Slumberfoot's sleep mode remains targetable and blocking; ten-second regeneration expiry does not wake it. S2 fixes source input-position recipients at attack startup. Radius centering, sleep-priority dispatch and pre-shield wake ordering remain explicit bounded mappings. Miss.Christine's talent observes actual consumed palsy stacks, never grants or passive decay. S1 uses accepted Arts damage for Neural injury. Her born S2 spirit retains current source ATK through movement and owner removal, with a source-selected after-arrival duration and end gate. Native lifetime/parent clock binding and the missing Back loop alias remain explicit limits.

Executor the Ex Foedere uses original facing-specific single/double attack events, one probability roll and one ammo expenditure per attack family. His final double-attack tail completes before the empty-ammo skill ends. S3 retains its own marked targets and skill modifiers through the separate end hit and cleanup. Native ammo-event dispatch, recovery caps and same-frame ordering remain explicit interpretations. Philae uses selected injury protection and Necrosis-input SP, a fifteen-second injury barrier and forty-second counter mode. Accepted incoming HP receipts select one delayed counter pulse per two-second cooldown; already attached pulses survive the owner's removal. Injury shield ordering, native receipt dispatch and the missing Back beginning alias remain explicit limits.

Windflit supplies original five-DP equipment with a facing picker, zero deployment slots, finite promotion stock, a two-device limit and a fifteen-second placement cooldown. The native Start must finish before its directional Caster/Supporter ATK aura takes effect. Equipment grants stack independently, and S1 forces SP through the equipped recipient's active/no-SP state. S2 boosts the equipment talent and replenishes one stock only on normal duration completion. Native current-target dispatch, attachment/lifetime phases and animation FSM transitions remain explicit limits. Blemishine keeps defensive-recovery SP from attacks, sleeping-target priority/damage, a charged S1 and separate delayed secondary heals. S3 coalesces accepted Physical/Arts outputs from one attack for its heal; S1's emitted spell can heal even when damage is cancelled. S2 releases Sleep after the original half-second hit and retains the selected ten-second mode independently of its beginning clip. Native event coalescence, Sequence dispatch, regeneration modifier semantics and secondary-heal phase remain bounded mappings.

Spuria supports both source skills and all ten ranks. S1 grants its timed deployment ASPD; S2 buffs herself and one eligible forward Sniper without retargeting. Her trait loses 1% maximum HP each second and stops at 1 HP. One talent roll selects extra damage, stun or DEF penetration; born extra damage cannot reroll. Original Attack/Skill loops and facing-specific hit events control projectile release. Accepted enemy-damage outputs and attack-family IDs approximate the native output event, and forward recipient tie-breaking is an explicit simulator interpretation. Recipient buffs keep their own duration if Spuria withdraws. Modules, native particles/audio and game-frame parity remain unsupported.

Robin uses both source skills, automatic trap replenishment, source initial supplies of 4/6/8 (plus potential bonuses), and total stored capacities of 6/8/10. Clips cost 3 DP, redeploy after 5 seconds, take no deployment slot, and require a ground tile without a ground enemy. Each fixed-direction Clip waits for its original .5-second entrance and .167-second impact event, then affects one ground victim with source physical damage and bind or radial push. Her normal ranged projectile can hit aerial targets. Owner withdrawal removes remaining Clips; redeployment refreshes initial supply. `data/arkpedia-robin-prefabs.json` retains six verified native bundle identities, original owner/token graphs, forty skill ranks, and the source bind/launch artwork. Bounded interpretations remain explicit: total stock combines the ready card with stacked cards; traps sample current owner ATK at placement because native inheritance timing is unrecovered; equal-frame contact ties use nearest centre then spawn order; control precedes damage and the device withdraws at impact. These choices are tested, not claims of native executable or frame parity. Separate native Unity effects/audio are not reproduced.

Frost uses both source skills, initial trap supply and automatic replenishment. Fixed-direction Welcome Mats cost 3 DP, redeploy after five seconds and occupy no deployment slots. The original Start entrance lasts .5 seconds; Attack_Begin strikes at its literal .1-second event. S1 deals selected-rank physical damage and stun; S2 deals trap damage and bind, then fires three owner projectiles when Frost can act and the victim is within her range. The owner's original Skill hit event starts that sequence, with the native .05-second spacing thereafter. Control or withdrawal cancels unreleased shots while fired projectiles continue. A device holds until its own control ends, then uses the original Attack_End dismissal. `data/arkpedia-frost-prefabs.json` retains six verified bundle identities, complete owner/token graphs, forty skill ranks and byte-for-byte original owner/token skeleton bindings. Explicit simulator bounds cover ATK transfer at placement, live host ATK at projectile impact, equal-frame contacts, interrupted burst replacement, attack-CD reset and control/damage dispatch. Modules, Unity effects/audio and native frame parity remain unsupported.

Surtr uses original facing-specific attack events, selected promotion/potential RES penetration and a one-use fatal survival timer: four/five seconds at E1 or eight/nine at E2, then forced withdrawal without retreat DP. S1 restores SP only when its own emitted attack kills its victim. S2 selects up to two current ground targets and applies its extra multiplier only to a single-target attack. S3 adds 5,000 HP, heals after the HP change and attacks up to four targets, with a rising HP drain and no manual cancellation. Withdrawal clears her owned timers; redeployment creates a fresh kit. Native bleed tick phase, event-versus-predelay ordering, selector dispatch and fatal callback arbitration remain explicit simulator bounds. Modules, audio and original Unity particle effects remain unsupported.

Selected skill animations use that skill's parsed Front/Back role. Literal form transitions honor reviewed alias speeds independently of attack windup and other actors. Missing dedicated clips do not borrow another skill's animation; attack-buff skills keep event-driven normal attacks. Projectile artwork, hook lines, shift travel and exact frame timing still need game comparison; these adapters do not establish full visual fidelity.

Squad setup stays available in portrait. Battles on phones and touch tablets require landscape: a rotation prompt blocks battle controls in portrait. Rotating back pauses combat and cancels unfinished deployment without spending DP; the squad and battle progress remain intact. Returning to landscape requires an explicit Start/Resume. Tall desktop windows with mouse controls remain supported.

Attack animations play once for each combat attack, then return to idle. Skills that reuse the normal attack animation (such as Melantha’s ATK buff) do not start attack loops without a combat event. Melantha’s normal attacks and active skill damage one enemy per attack, even when enemies overlap.

Combat runs at a fixed 30Hz with seeded randomness. Rendering cannot change the number of combat ticks. A hidden page pauses instead of trying to catch up. Deployment entrance/death clips can finish cosmetically while paused; combat, skill durations and attack animations remain paused.

Flametail keeps one pending follow-up per evasion family, a strongest nonstacking Kazimierz dodge aura and all three source skills. S2 retains its input victims for two separate waves and updates its ten-second physical-dodge field every 0.2 seconds; ordinary combat tokens can receive that field. S3 changes attack interval, block and dodge while generating eight periodic DP. Source target-bound follow-up lifetime, minimum-one victim at zero block and native command/attachment phases are recorded explicitly. Animation endings do not add an invented action or SP lock.

Alanna uses the original Nutty device without an invented attack or HP gauge. Its native Start is presentation; the thirty-second effect lifetime starts at deployment, extended by selected passive S1. Owner birth adds finite promotion stock, capped at three; S2 refills one only on normal completion. Overlapping devices from one owner share one recipient talent, with current-mode DEF penetration evaluated at damage time. Source marker cadence, cached projectile reevaluation and foreign-owner priority remain explicit mappings. Saileach relocates her aura to a stationary S2/S3 banner; a stopped banner does not restore the owner-centered aura until that mode ends, with S2 DEF/regeneration and S3 slow, Fragile and a separately born blast. Her unused next-ordinary-deployment discount clears with its owner and is consumed only after a successful eligible spawn. Native Parallel center sharing, tile choice, card ordering, collider and callback phases remain explicit simulator bounds. Neither adapter imports unrecovered Unity flag particles.

## Data and coverage

`data/arkpedia-mvp.json` records full source commits for public `arkpedia-data`, Global game tables, icon and operator-art assets, and SD models. `tools/arkpedia/build-mvp.mjs --refresh` updates that compact snapshot; it requires the sibling `arkpedia-sd-assets` checkout and `gh` access. Import/publish complete SD models first, then regenerate. The generator rejects conditional stages, fixed squads, unfamiliar geometry/route shapes and missing models. The runtime validates all loadouts and never accepts caller-provided stats.

The regular-stage roster is opt-in through `shared/arkpedia/operators.js` and `enemies.js`. The build tool and runtime reject unknown operators, skill IDs, talent blackboard keys and enemies; spawns must have supported enemy records. Inherited kits remain disabled: Stronghold's `chess_` units have mode-specific builds, automatic-operation rules and modifiers. A hand-authored kit there is a migration candidate, not proof of ordinary-stage compatibility.

`data/arkpedia-roster-target.json` separately pins the full CN target: 429 operators, or 431 operator forms including Amiya Guard and Medic, at CN commit `a550f5e048bb94e7cdefc6eb97a4091f0c4c7add`. The Global snapshot below is only the current source scope, not the full project goal. Coverage reports both counts and every unimplemented CN/form ID. Refresh the target with `node tools/arkpedia/roster-target.mjs --refresh`; this never enables new combat kits or changes reviewed Global source pins.

`data/arkpedia-coverage.json` audits the pinned Global catalogue: 374 obtainable operators, 817 skills and 1,552 enemy database IDs. 336 operator forms, 707 skills and two basic enemies are currently playable: all 90 one- through four-stars, 167 five-stars and 79 six-stars. The full pinned target still has 95 unimplemented forms, including 57 outside this older Global snapshot. Two-star builds and supports use E0 level 30, with no skill, SP gauge or activation button. Yato's redeployment talent combines with her potential reduction. Noir Corne gains source HP/DEF bonuses and blocks three while attacking one target. Rangers prioritizes aerial targets and gains his anti-air ATK multiplier; synthetic aerial-target tests do not enable additional enemy types. Durin gains Arts-only dodge, and 12F gains physical-only dodge. These talents unlock at level 30. 12F uses the inherited Arts splash profile; its base radius, like Lava's and Catapult's, still needs client-prefab verification. It identifies 265 skills and 210 enemy IDs with inherited implementation candidates, including stats-only entries whose notes may describe missing mechanics. All 374 original operator models are imported in the published asset catalogue. Coverage reads that committed catalogue independently of combat support: art alone does not enable an operator. Original Front-only and single-skeleton exceptions retain their source identities; incomplete animation roles are not invented. It separately records placeholder effects and unverified game fidelity. It is an offline report; the battle does not load the full catalogue.

To import another reviewed batch and reproduce coverage:

```sh
# Register and implement/test regular-stage mechanics before enabling an operator.
# Front/Back models retain their original pinned files; this parses attachment,
# clip and hit metadata with the same Spine runtime as the browser.
node tools/arkpedia/import-operators.mjs --ids char_240_wyvern,char_209_ardign,char_278_orchid --commit d0b5af0b004b044d322397ce5ae79632b6d9fcdd --pma false
# Optional pinned Git source avoids directory API rate limits; uncommitted files are ignored.
# Add --source-root ../arkpedia-sd-assets/.cache/arknights-resource to that command.
# Reinspect existing pairs for every selected skill without redownloading files:
node tools/arkpedia/import-operators.mjs --inspect-existing --commit d0b5af0b004b044d322397ce5ae79632b6d9fcdd --pma false
# Validate and publish the sibling asset repo, then pin its committed manifest.
node tools/arkpedia/build-mvp.mjs
npm run coverage:arkpedia
```

The complete original catalogue is pinned to asset commit `20bebf2e493916a68e9586e509c8147f4027db33`. Its separate `operator-catalogue.json` records pinned Global character/skin source fingerprints and model identities; all 2,226 original operator files were checked against exact datamine Git blobs. `--fixed-front-ids` and `--single-model-ids` require explicit original exceptions, and `--source-directory-map` handles the verified Liskarm folder spelling without changing the character ID. The battle still downloads only the chosen squad's models.

Blending is an explicit import setting, followed by browser QA. The importer does not claim that parsed clips have been compared frame-for-frame with the game. Coverage regeneration uses the existing pinned source cache and rejects a source-pin mismatch; a fresh checkout first needs `build:arkpedia-data` to fetch its source tables.

### Source behaviour templates and effects

The pinned Global `gamedata/battle/buff_template_data.json` contains 5,468 templates and 916 action types. `shared/arkpedia/behavior.js` independently implements the reviewed `ModifyCost` and self-cast `HealViaMaxHpRatio` variants for `ON_BUFF_START`. It compiles the entire template before execution, rejects unknown actions/events/fields and resolves all operands before changing combat. Cross-unit source/owner rules, nested conditions, other events, priorities, buff lifetime/stacking and particle effects are not supported by this interpreter.

Fang and Vanilla now execute the original `charge_cost` template once at skill activation. Their prefab-to-template bindings are verified against the official Global skill bundle, rather than inferred from their skill names. Cardigan uses a native HP-ratio heal ability in the client and retains its explicit adapter; the unrelated `instant_heal[hp_ratio]` buff is tested in isolation, not assigned to Cardigan. No additional operators are enabled by this change.

`data/arkpedia-behavior-audit.json` records action/event counts, first rejection reasons, accepted isolated templates and the two live operator bindings. Fifteen templates compile in the restricted self-cast context, including ten empty/no-action records; only five contain actions. Acceptance of a buff alone is not support for its containing skill or operator.

```sh
# Fetch only the snapshot's immutable template table, verify SHA-256 and audit.
# This does not refresh the playable snapshot or source commits.
npm run audit:arkpedia-behaviors -- --fetch
# With the pinned cache present, this command is offline:
npm run audit:arkpedia-behaviors
```

`data/arkpedia-skill-prefabs.json` records checksum-verified original prefab bindings and an inventory of the skill/projectile/common/buff bundles. The `common_charge_cost_start_01`, `common_ignite_attack` and `common_heal_hit_01` roots exist in `battle/prefabs/effects/common.ab`. Their assets include Unity particles, materials, animation clips and trails; an inventory alone does not establish runtime support.

```sh
node tools/arkpedia/stages/fetch-bundles.mjs --version 26-09-23-17-49-43_b9cc4a --skills-only
.cache/map-env/bin/python tools/arkpedia/stages/export-skill-bindings.py --bundles .cache/arkpedia/map-source/ab --manifest .cache/arkpedia/map-source/hot_update_list.json --templates .cache/arkpedia/buff_template_data.json --out data/arkpedia-skill-prefabs.json --version 26-09-23-17-49-43_b9cc4a
```

The extractor compares both reviewed template action lists with the original Unity template holder and records exact source bundle hashes. Rebuilding requires the template-table hash to match that evidence. A source refresh which changes it fails until the bindings are re-extracted and reviewed. No code from the newly researched battle engine, DPS calculator or Myrtle is included; their unresolved reuse terms do not affect this independent implementation.

### Original charge-cost activation particles

Fang and Vanilla's skill-start events now render the five original billboard emitters in `common_charge_cost_start_01`. The immutable asset pack includes two lossless game textures, separate RGB/alpha gradients, unweighted Hermite size curves, burst counts, radial cone/sphere emission, angular velocity and the birth sub-emitter. Texture and pack hashes are verified before use. A failed load is labelled; the renderer does not invent replacement particles. Cosmetic randomness is separate from combat RNG. Effects follow the battle clock, freeze during pause, speed up with combat and are disposed on reset/expiry.

Only the activation burst is implemented. The follow-up `common_charge_cost_01` flight to the DP counter uses custom motion/noise/trail scripts and remains deferred. The current body anchor at 0.6 tile height, 60 Hz velocity-limit damping and Pixi shader rendering are approximations; recorded game comparison is still required. ATK/heal effects and projectiles remain placeholders. No additional operators are enabled.

```sh
node tools/arkpedia/stages/fetch-bundles.mjs --version 26-09-23-17-49-43_b9cc4a --dp-effect-only
.cache/map-env/bin/python tools/arkpedia/stages/export-dp-effect.py --bundles .cache/arkpedia/map-source/ab --manifest .cache/arkpedia/map-source/hot_update_list.json --out .cache/arkpedia/dp-pack --version 26-09-23-17-49-43_b9cc4a
```

The exporter verifies four original bundles and rejects new enabled modules, weighted curves and unknown material variants. Publish the pack in the sibling asset repository before rebuilding the simulator's pin. A source-effect preview at `/arkpedia/effect-preview.html` uses the same renderer and actual Fang/Vanilla skill activation events, with replay and timeline scrubbing for visual review. It is separate from gameplay.

Routes come from the existing Arkpedia stage browser's `buildPlaybackPaths` output: public points, cumulative distances, waits and movement scale, not private app source. The simulator generator retains that export only while its geometry hash matches. After a geometry refresh it requires a new export, rather than silently using different routes:

```sh
# From the private Arkpedia app worktree, after refreshing the simulator source cache:
npx tsx scripts/build/export-stage-simulator-routes.ts ../arkpedia-stage-simulator/.cache/arkpedia/geometry.json /tmp/arkpedia-stage-routes.json 0-1
# From this public simulator checkout:
node tools/arkpedia/build-mvp.mjs --routes /tmp/arkpedia-stage-routes.json
```

Dropping a portrait onto a tile opens the direction picker without deploying or spending DP. Start a separate drag from the picker centre, swipe toward the intended direction, and release to deploy. Releasing within the centre's dead zone keeps placement pending; Escape, Cancel and pointer cancellation never spend DP. Arrow keys preview facing and Enter confirms; clicking a facing arrow also confirms. Terrain, occupancy, DP and cooldown are checked again at confirmation. Paths can be toggled independently of operator range; the wait point is marked with a ring.

Enemy sprites face their horizontal movement, retain that facing through waits and vertical route segments, and turn toward a blocker when attacking. Their initial facing comes from the route rather than the engine's fixed deployment direction.

Deployed operators show a green SP gauge below HP. Ready manual skills show a yellow lightning diamond above the bars; select that operator, then activate the skill. Automatic skills trigger through the combat engine and do not show a manual-ready marker. The gauge turns orange and drains during a timed skill (or tracks remaining ammo); passive skills and operators without skills have no SP gauge. All indicators follow the paused simulation clock and disappear on retreat or death. Gauge placement samples the original resting pose once, avoiding distant effect attachments in source skeleton headers and movement during attacks.

Selecting an operator opens a left-side inspector with pinned base artwork, build level, live ATK/DEF/RES/block, HP, SP, skill description and activation/retreat controls. It overlays the battlefield without changing its dimensions and disappears while dragging or choosing deployment direction. Portrait phones use a compact panel above the deployment shelf; short landscape views keep art and independently scrolling details side by side, with retreat/skill buttons anchored below. Close or Escape dismisses the inspector without retreating the operator. Automatic skills and operators without skills have no manual activation button.

This is a playable prototype, **not full game compatibility**. Timings, movement scale, projectile flight and animation wind-up need recorded in-game comparison. Modules, most enemy abilities, other stages, the remaining five-/six-star operators, special modes, replay persistence and a worker are not implemented. Deepcolor, Roberta and Beanstalk have their explicit summon/device rules; that does not enable other summon systems. A model existing does not mean its mechanics are supported. The old Arkpedia range-preview/playback tool is retained.

Tests compare every unblocked movement tick with the exported viewer paths/waits, and cover projected facing/range perimeter geometry, source routing, stats/caps, support, fullscreen/terrain/DP checks, retreat/redeployment, Fang's clear, healing, manual skills and life loss. Upstream tests continue to verify the inherited combat primitives separately.

### Iana: Mirage, substitute and both skills

Iana supports both skills and all 20 source ranks. The deployed Mirage never attacks. ### Gnosis: full source kit with bounded continuous dispatch

Gnosis supports all three source skills and all 30 ranks. Ordinary attacks and S1 use the original facing hit events (.467 and .367 seconds) with the source animation cap. S1's second projectile follows the native .2-second trigger spacing, rather than the next literal animation event. Source CAST selection can replace a dead target; an all-dead input refunds an unlaunched cast. The SP lock ends when the last issued projectile becomes invalid, including a target lost during flight. Cold applies before the shared damage output. Independent layers retain one pairing credit each; two accepted layers produce Freeze using the longer post-resistance lifetime. Frozen immunity prevents pairing. Multiple Cold layers supply one attack-speed penalty, which is suppressed while Frozen. The charged branch handles already-Cold and Frozen-immune recipients separately from direct Freeze.

The original Begin, eventless Loop and End roles are delivered. The original continuous RangedAttack dispatcher is still unrecovered: the adapter repeats immediate-release projectiles at source BAT/ASPD after Begin and reserves the End hit window within the skill duration. It releases before this engine's aura-expiry phase, with SP blocked through the remaining End pose. These are tested local timings, not recovered native executable or game-frame parity.

The source-owned unresistable Freeze holder detaches on range exit, skill end or withdrawal and keeps one RES reduction after finite Freeze expires. Kjerag Resist activates after the source ten-second delay for eligible deployed operators carrying the nation tag, including Gnosis; withdrawal removes his contribution.

### Texas the Omertosa: full source kit with explicit born-sequence timing

Texas supports all three source skills and all 30 ranks. S1 adds selected ATK, physical attacks, silence and fixed Arts DoT with independent source ownership. Levitate is applied before checking that aerial multiplier. Dodged hits cannot silence; successful shield-only receipts can. Her second talent applies owned, nonstacking Weightless in current attack range, immediately on entry and with the native .4-second HP refresh. The native GT comparison requires strictly more than 80% HP. Range exit, withdrawal and death remove only her own Weightless contribution.

S1 stores its source charge count and enhances the next attack against up to two targets. It applies Levitate only when that attack actually emits one projectile. A second victim disappearing during flight does not change the emitted count. S2 uses a .5-second ASPD-scaled windup and nine independent random-target releases spaced by the native .05-second interval, followed by each bolt's fixed .05-second start delay and speed 11. Control, skill expiry and withdrawal cancel unreleased shots; emitted bolts survive cleanup. S2 retains its original Front loop even when deployed facing up.

S3 replaces ordinary attacks with its own attack clock, including attacks with no enemies present. Following the native .5-second windup, three independently delayed whirlwinds start in the centre and adjacent lanes, move at speed 1, query a 1×1 square and each hit one eligible enemy. Damage rises along the preserved native curve, reaches its maximum near 1.77 seconds, samples current ATK and applies Levitate before the aerial talent. Facing determines each lane's origin and direction. Unreleased windups cancel on interruption; already emitted winds survive withdrawal without the owner's aerial talent.

`data/arkpedia-hoolheyak-prefabs.json` preserves five independently hash-verified original bundles, 128 native components, eight exact templates, the pinned Weightless/Silence database closures, all ranks/ranges and both official-to-delivered facing chains. Prior 331 operator records, 24 tokens and all 799 SD records remain unchanged. Native non-finite floats retain the explicit string `"Infinity"` in strict JSON. [PRTS attachment notes](https://prts.wiki/w/%E9%9C%8D%E5%B0%94%E6%B5%B7%E9%9B%85), revision 434969, corroborate the emitted-projectile condition, aerial hit order, independent lanes, current-ATK sampling and withdrawal behavior.

The compiled native mover remains unresolved: the original projectile has a four-second lifetime, while PRTS describes disappearance at five tiles of centre travel. This adapter preserves the literal four-second limit without snapping to an endpoint; final travel distance is not certified. The moving square query runs at the simulator's 30 Hz rather than native frame parity. Original projectile/whirlwind particles, sound, modules and native animation-to-damage dispatch remain unfinished. S3 uses the native .5-second release contract, independently of the delivered Spine loop's .867-second hit event. Visuals remain tracked placeholder bolts/orbs.

All 56 focused Ho'olheyak tests pass; the combined historical-deferral regression passes 81 tests. The full regression passes 8,430 tests, nine skipped, no failures (8,439 total). Local landscape browser checks used E2 Lv90/P1/zero trust, all three skills at M3 and natural DP. S1 showed its automatic next-attack readiness and one defeated enemy with no escapes. S2 charged to 30/30, activated with a 15-second countdown and displayed its original Front loop despite facing up. S3 charged to 60/60, activated with expanded range and a 44-second countdown, and reached three defeated enemies with no escapes during that check. These are short combat-flow checks, not full-stage clears or original-effect parity. Artwork, original chibi and skill icons loaded with no observed console warnings/errors.

Coverage is now 332/431 pinned forms and 695 skills. Of the 99 remaining forms, 42 belong to the older Global snapshot and 57 are outside it.


### Ebenholz: shared charges and Old Day Remnants

Ebenholz supports all three skills and all 30 source ranks. Normal attacks retain one ground or aerial input, emit the primary projectile and release up to three stored attacks. ### Lin: all three skills and Crystal Barrier

Lin supports Elegance, Shelter and Riving Lighttails at all 30 source ranks. The idle Phalanx stance has the selected DEF/RES modifiers and does not attack. S1 is a cancellable infinite toggle with additive attack interval, ATK and Slow on every selected ground or aerial target. S2 grants selected ASPD and lower taunt for 25 seconds; allied Crystal Barriers persist after leaving her range and are removed when Shelter ends. S3 changes ATK/range and multiplies only the barrier threshold, retaining the source attack-only kill filter and .2-second refresh lifetime. Ordinary shatter damage cannot recursively trigger that refresh.

Barriers use selected promotion/potential values, fixed resistance per damage instance and an independent reform timer across mode changes. Their stun precedes Arts damage. The local mapping subtracts the threshold after mitigation and before ordinary shields, passes excess damage, and shatters on strict overflow. The native `BlockDamage` and `dynamic < 0` fields are retained; the closed implementation, strict equality versus translated text, aura blast origins, priority and coincident callbacks remain documented local policies. Shrouded Strength uses the selected probability and can recover SP from fully blocked damage, subject to active-skill/no-SP gates. Direct HP loss bypasses the barrier and cannot trigger that SP gain.

Original Front/Back bytes already exist at the unchanged SD pin. S1 and S3 retain their literal .4/.333-second hit events and native playback cap; S3 uses the original A/B/C clips with a seeded local selection. S2's literal loop has no hit event despite the native ability waiting for one: local attacks release with zero windup while the loop continues. That event dispatcher is not an exact reconstruction of Unity. Native barrier/shatter particles, audio, modules and game-frame parity remain unfinished.

`data/arkpedia-lin-prefabs.json` preserves five independently verified bundles, 115 full native components, nine reachable templates, all 30 ranks and both original skeleton chains. `tools/arkpedia/verify-lin.py` compares these records, tables, template-holder bytes and imported skeletons with the pinned originals. All prior 333 operator records and 25 token records remain unchanged. The asset repository and its 801-record manifest are unchanged; the runtime snapshot adds only Lin’s existing Front/Back records to its lazy-load subset. The older caster audit remains historical evidence, superseded for Lin by this standalone adapter and its documented timing limits. Coverage is 334/431 forms and 701 skills; 97 forms remain, 40 from the older Global snapshot and 57 outside it.

All 47 focused Lin tests pass. The full regression passes 8,531 tests, nine skipped, no failures (8,540 total). Browser checks used E2 Lv90/P1/zero trust and M3 with natural DP/SP: idle stats were 849 ATK, 726 DEF and 35 RES; S1 displayed 1,358 ATK and toggled off through the HUD; S2 continued its original loop and defeated four enemies during the observed active window; S3 displayed 2,547 ATK, expanded range and two attack kills, then manual cancellation restored the defensive stance and zero SP. No console warnings/errors were observed. These were focused skill playtests, not claims of zero-escape full-stage clears.

### Ulpianus: source verification and move lifetime foundation (not playable yet)

### Lappland straight-cone sparks and local curl replay

`native-moving-particles.js` now supports source initial speed and straight base-cone emission, preserving the native radius, thickness, shape scale/rotation and collapsed axes. The strict stationary factory still rejects nonzero start speed. Angled cones, directed/randomized shapes and non-random arc/radius modes remain unsupported.

`native-particle-noise.js` implements a deterministic high-quality curl-of-Perlin field with analytic derivatives. Unity describes its [noise algorithm as curl noise built from Perlin samples](https://docs.unity3d.com/2021.3/Documentation/Manual/PartSysNoiseModule.html); the [curl-noise paper](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~rbridson/docs/bridson-siggraph2007-curlnoise.pdf) provides the vector-field construction. Neither reference provides the game client's native permutation tables, coordinate phase or particle-module execution order. This implementation is **a local inspection replay**, not recovered Unity native code.

`native-particle-motion.js` samples the original strength, position amount, frequency, scroll, octaves, octave multiplier/scale and damping controls. It also samples the original speed-limit curve and dampen fraction. Supported source controls are high quality, shared axes, no remap/rotation/size noise, a constant scroll speed, a magnitude limit and zero drag. Other controls fail explicitly. The documented local mapping uses independent seeded Perlin fields, scroll along field Z, inverse-frequency damping, and a fixed 1/60-second replay. Each step evaluates curl drift, damps the combined velocity toward the source speed limit, advances position, and retains the limited base-velocity residual without accumulating curl as an invented acceleration. Partial steps use the corresponding fractional damping. **Field tables, scroll axis, timestep, damping conversion and module ordering remain unverified against Unity/game frames.**

The ordinary wolf's two spark systems now play with their original sprites, colors, sizes, lifetimes, prewarm, source cone and speed/noise controls. Each ordinary wolf root has eleven inspected components; only its two unresolved mesh references remain blocked. The S3 wolf's trails and time-emitted world-space sparks can now replay supplied movement history (see below); its distance-emitted particles remain unplayed. The unchanged source-resource manifest still lists nine unresolved resources across the full effect closure.

### Lappland source trails with recorded movement

The isolated original-effect inspector now constructs camera-facing stretch ribbons from the original `TrailRenderer` settings. All 27 pinned trail components use View alignment, Stretch textures, zero corner/end-cap vertices and no generated lighting data. The four S3 wolf layers preserve their separate source materials, textures, shader programs, widths (approximately 0.60/0.52/0.52/0.65), lifetimes (0.7/0.8/0.7/0.6 seconds), minimum world-point spacing (0.01) and sorting orders. Original shader arithmetic remains unchanged.

`shared/arkpedia/native-effect-trail.js` accepts explicit chronological world-position history. It filters movement by source minimum distance, retains point birth clocks during stops/emission pauses, removes points at their source lifetime and samples the original width curve/color gradient along normalized cumulative ribbon length. The local ribbon uses two vertices per retained point with an averaged tangent, camera-facing sides and Stretch UVs; source material properties supply texture scaling/offsets and dissolve/scroll controls. Rewinding reconstructs from history instead of retaining future geometry. Dynamic GPU buffers are reused when their size is unchanged and released before resizing.

The inspector's **Movement JSON** input accepts an array of `{time, position: [x, y, z]}` records beginning at time zero, in the original effect's world-coordinate axes. Positions are explicit root offsets; interpolation is linear and clamps to the first/last position. Loading movement also updates original mesh/particle poses and world-space particle birth positions. Clear movement restores the static original pose; static poses produce no artificial trail. `effectReview.setTrajectory(samples)` provides the same interface for a later recorded battle-motion integration. Motion inputs are limited to 20,000 ordered finite samples and the file input to 2 MB.

Unity's [Trail Renderer documentation](https://docs.unity3d.com/2021.3/Documentation/Manual/class-TrailRenderer.html) describes world-unit point spacing/lifetime and width/color sampling along trail length; [Stretch](https://docs.unity3d.com/2021.3/Documentation/ScriptReference/LineTextureMode.html) maps a texture once along its length. The **specific point-expiry boundary, lack of interpolated expired-tail shortening, head-at-last-accepted-point policy, normalized-length direction/UV orientation, averaged joins and camera-parallel fallback are explicit local replay mappings**. They are not recovered Unity-native implementations. The review fixture is numerical test motion, not a datamined wolf flight path. Unsupported alignment, texture modes, rounded caps/corners, lighting and automatic destruction fail explicitly. Native script movement/Animator dispatch, game camera mapping and compiled game-frame parity remain unverified.

### Lappland S3 world-space spark replay

The two S3 `spark01`/`spark02` time emitters now play from their original source settings and textures. Their simulation space is World rather than the ordinary wolf's Local space. `createMovingParticles.sample(time, {frameAt})` therefore requires an explicit birth-frame callback when speed limiting or noise is active in world space. Each callback returns separate spawn and movement matrices; source Shape-only scaling changes the spawn transform without silently scaling movement. The inspector obtains those matrices from the original hierarchy/explicit clip and the supplied movement offsets at each physical birth time. Prewarm births before time zero use the explicit start pose.

`particleBirthFrame` transforms the original shape point and initial velocity into world coordinates before motion replay. Curl noise and speed limiting then sample the evolving world point rather than translating a completed local-noise path. The result carries an explicit `worldPosition`; the renderer consumes it once, preserving already-born particles as the emitter translates. Reverse scrubbing reconstructs both original birth inputs and world-field motion. The renderer still rejects animated rotation/scale of world emitter ancestors; linear velocity combined with turbulence, arbitrary field-space conversion and those changing transform frames are not silently approximated.

Six other world-noise profiles still need distance emission. ### Lappland recorded-distance sparks and spherical smoke

`native-particle-lifecycle.js` merges constant-rate distance births with time emission and bursts before applying the shared capacity, lifetime and preview identity rules. Callers must supply ordered world-position history starting at physical time zero. Births occur at successive accumulated path-distance thresholds, interpolated along recorded segments; turns preserve accumulated distance and stationary intervals add none. Start delay, simulation speed and nonloop duration bound the physical interval. Prewarm holds the explicit start pose without inventing movement before zero. Original birth transforms retain particles behind the moving emitter.

[Unity's emission reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/2021.3/Documentation/Manual/PartSysEmissionModule.html) establishes particles per travelled unit, while its [shape reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/2021.3/Documentation/Manual/PartSysShapeModule.html) describes sphere directions and radius thickness. The deterministic random stream, shell sampling, distance threshold phase, time/distance/burst tie order, prewarm motion policy and interpolation between recorded world positions remain **documented local mappings**, not recovered compiled Unity scheduling. ### Reusable original-effect player

`public/arkpedia/native-effect-player.js` now owns the source renderer previously embedded in the Lappland inspector. `createNativeEffectLibrary({three, pack, animations, shaders, loadTexture})` shares verified original texture loads and returns independently disposable instances through `await library.create(rootName)`. Each instance exposes its source pose, group, component records and `update(seconds, {camera, clip, trajectory})`. The caller supplies the clock, original-coordinate camera and render pass. The player creates no DOM, renderer, animation loop, combat timer or camera framing. The inspector now uses this same implementation.

Each root owns its geometry, particle clone pools, animated material values and trails. Shader matrix uniforms bind the camera passed by the caller's actual render pass. Retiring a root removes it from its parent and releases all of its GPU geometry/materials without disposing shared textures. Library shutdown retires every root, disposes shared textures and rejects creations still awaiting a texture; late decoded textures are released. Failed texture loads can retry. Shader compilation releases temporary GL handles and resets a borrowed renderer context even on failure.

Strict creation rejects roots with unplayed components and cleans up the failed instance. The inspector explicitly opts into diagnostic partial inspection. The recovered particle renderers' repeated identical material slots are accepted only with their own particle TrailModule disabled; differing slots, enabled particle trails and unsupported mesh multi-material paths remain explicit blockers. Original materials, source samplers, shaders, hierarchy, particle mappings and trail mappings are retained.

The instance group must remain in original Unity coordinates. A transformed group or ancestor fails before updating: applying a board transform to finished geometry would otherwise leave noise sampling in the wrong coordinate space. **The stage camera/coordinate bridge, controller-to-instance activation, public factory integration and original asset publication remain open.** This API is not yet connected to the public battle renderer. It does not implement native Animator/FSM dispatch, mount heights, heading, effect retirement tails or compiled game-frame parity.

### Original effects in the private stage fixture

`native-stage-camera.js` maps the existing board camera into original Unity effect coordinates without transforming the source geometry. Board `(column,row,height)` maps to source `(x,y,z) = (column,height,row)`. `lappland-stage-effects.js` observes active cruise segments from the source-bound controller recorder. Each segment owns an independent original S3 root and follows the last observed motion sample. Pending asset loads cannot resurrect retired roots. The layer changes no combat, skill charge, event or RNG state, and preserves the caller's render clearing policy and board depth buffer. Original materials using Always/disabled depth testing still ignore depth, as authored.

### Thorns the Lodestar private S3 polygon execution review

`prepareThornsS3` adds an executable private review path for all ten ranks. Natural SP and manual activation use the selected source record; passive range and ordinary Front/Back `Skill_3_Loop` behavior remain in the shared core. Anchor candidates use lowest current block count then latest deployment, limited by `max_target_token`; devices/tokens, target-free, heal-free, isolated and out-of-range units cannot be anchors. With no other candidates, activation still creates a point at the owner tile.

The geometry module uses the native collider offset/line half-width `0.32499998807907104`. It forms a convex hull, drops interior/collinear anchors, translates polygon edges outward, and handles point, narrow strip and convex-polygon body intersection. Parallel translated edges meet at mitered corners; it does not replace the region with a circle or bounding box. Large hit areas use polygon/rectangle intersection. Eligible allied blockers inside the region confer membership on their blocked enemies, while devices do not.

Each region has independent cached ATK, lifetime and ramp state, persists after owner/anchor retreat, hits ground and air, and causes sourceless Arts damage. ATK/DEF/RES reductions use the highest native ATK-magnitude priority across active fields, with weaker-field fallback rather than multiplied debuffs. All ready field claims refresh before each damage receipt, so owner hook order cannot let a weaker cast ignore a stronger ready reduction. Damage from overlapping casts adds. Recipient death/exit, control, owner hiding/removal and battle completion have cleanup checks.

**This is private execution evidence, not finished public Thorns support.** The source preserves separate polygon-creator and Token dispatch, a half-second start delay, a one-second reached-delay and incrementer components. The current review samples anchors/cached ATK at the original capped 0.7-second Token event, makes the region ready half a second later, starts its duration at readiness, and samples the ramp on whole intervals after readiness. That ordering is an explicit local mapping requiring original-game comparison; the preserved creator dispatch and reached-delay semantics are not claimed as verified. Flat strip endpoint caps and `1e-9` boundary tolerance are also local geometry mappings. Original native particles/audio, mounts, modules and compiled frame parity remain unverified.

- S1/S2/S3 use separate dragon records. Their native terrain rules are melee/ranged/melee, all require a facing, and each lower-form summon occupies one deployment slot. Dragon parameters use the native `2.` prefix. Higher ranks store two charges. The separate Recycle ability has a serialized 1.2-second pre-delay, a strict below-50%-HP check, then ordered forced withdrawal and card recharge. This is not immediate unconditional recycling.
- S3 preserves five native modes: lower ordinary, lower active, higher ordinary, higher active and consumed. Fusion has same-host and lower-form validators, direction checks and source selector postFilter35. Its ordered actions transfer deployment volume, switch the survivor to the appropriate higher mode, restore HP despite healing restrictions and remove the absorbed dragon through consumed mode4. Higher-form stats use selected token blackboard modifiers, including additive +2 block and +.8 seconds base attack time, rather than treating every modifier as multiplicative.
- S3's periodic Arts damage uses Ling as its damage source and the dragon as the area centre. The source `x-5` range includes the centre and four adjacent tiles. Skill ranks preserve their own ATK/DEF bonuses, durations and half-second interval. Mode changes and end-of-skill card gain remain separate source actions.
- The summon-departure talent is serialized on `ON_OWNER_KILLED`, with a separate SP trigger and an infinite stacking ATK buff capped at five. Native withdrawal/absorption event dispatch and trigger clocks require runtime mapping and review; the extraction does not claim that every callback already executes in the simulator.

Lower dragons retain 11/30-second Attack events, the ranged dragon's Skill event is .5 seconds, and the higher dragon's `Attack_02` event is .5 seconds. `Born_2` maps to `Start_02` with its own 8/30-second event. All five original projectile trees retain speed ten. Each default dragon's root/controller/animator/skeleton/atlas/FaceSwitcher chain is recovered directly from the original token bundle. Higher-form aliases and animator hooks are preserved; outfit variants are not substituted. Owner Front/Back skeletons match pinned model commit `d0b5af0b004b044d322397ce5ae79632b6d9fcdd`. ### Shu ordinary combat, Sowing and talents

It neither hits another enemy in the same tile nor redirects a failed hit to a neighbour.
- Accepted direct healing sows the target tile and four neighbours, including zero-overheal receipts. Tile eligibility preserves the source buildable-or-ground-passable condition. Repeated healing adds no duplicate per-recipient recovery or Sanctuary. Normal deployment does not sow a tile without the unsupported module.
- Sowing maintains original per-promotion/potential HP recovery and Sanctuary while Shu remains deployed. Allies and summons can enter or leave the stored tiles; removal of a recipient leaves the tile state for later occupants. Owner removal/battle end clears the tiles and derived effects. Passive no-heal/HEAL_FREE do not reject the HP-recovery attribute, although they still reject direct healing. Sanctuary selects the strongest source and leaves true damage/HP loss unchanged.
- The shared regeneration path now bypasses healing multipliers and heal-output callbacks. This applies to natural HP recovery and explicit regeneration receipts; ordinary healing still uses its modifiers and listeners. It prevents a regeneration tick from causing another Sowing trigger. Regeneration exposes a separate frozen `regenerated` receipt after HP/credit settlement for observation. Critically wounded enemies retain a distinct recovery prohibition, including explicit regeneration calls. The distinction is present in the native `HP_RECOVERY_PER_SEC` modifier and is corroborated by [Shu's documented regeneration behavior](https://arknights.wiki.gg/wiki/Shu).
- Field talent auras count deployed operators by original class, excluding summons/devices. Three different classes add maximum HP while preserving current HP ratio; three of the same class add ASPD. The two checks are independent and refresh on deployment/removal and the simulation tick.
- A separate squad controller counts unique Sui character records in the squad, including undeployed Shu and squad members. With at least four, deployed operators receive the source ATK percentage and independent four-second SP clocks from each recipient's deployment. Stopped recovery loses that pulse rather than receiving delayed SP later. Shu's retreat removes her field effects but leaves the deck bonus; battle end clears the squad controller and its hooks.

### Shu selected skills and teleport diagnostics (2026-10-12)

`server/sim/content/arkpedia-shu-skills.js` extends the separately reviewed core with an explicit diagnostic skill contract.
