- S1 is an automatic charged heal. The native selector includes a friendly character at exactly half HP, retains that trigger input, caps the original `Attack_2` clock at normal speed and stops SP recovery during the cast. It cancels a failed search without spending a charge, refunds an input that died before release, and does not redirect a hidden/stale input. Legal overheal still emits a healing output and sows tiles. Control interrupts an unreleased heal.
- S2 changes the attack mode into two-target healing, expands the range, adds the selected ATK percentage, adds the serialized BAT and block modifiers, and scales both Sowing attributes. Existing sowed recipients refresh at skill start/end instead of keeping old Sanctuary values. The source healing primary input is retained while remaining CAST recipients use the shared strike-time selector mapping. Ordinary enemy damage stops while this mode runs. End/removal cancels pending casts and removes excess block capacity after the skill modifier is removed.
- S3 uses its original begin/end and two attack clips. It dispatches a single ground Physical attack through the common accepted-attack path, then invokes independent healing; a dodged hit still heals. Without an enemy it can use the healing path alone. Fresh accepted heals immediately refresh the sowed-tile enemy listener. Current enemy presence applies the source ATK/ASPD bonus once, including isolated friendly characters/tokens and excluding devices. Leaving the sowed area removes that presence bonus without removing an existing teleport mark.
- S3 marks retain the first entered root tile for the source skill's lifetime. The source `FilterRootTileOffset GE` action uses a nearest-centre root-tile Manhattan mapping and returns the enemy to the recorded tile centre, without releasing a block relation, changing speed, restarting passed route checkpoints or clearing the current wait. The native mark-denial buff and `BE_TELEPORTED` action immunity are distinct. The metric, inclusive threshold, mark lifetime and path preservation are corroborated by [PRTS's Shu skill notes](https://prts.wiki/w/%E9%BB%8D).
- Optional movement observers run after an accepted route/attract/fear/displacement segment and before blocking or exit consumes it. They trace crossed roots, so an enemy cannot skip a sowed tile or teleport threshold just because it moved several tiles in one simulation tick. Relocation ends that tick's remaining movement and replans the current leg on the next tick. Disappearance removes the mark immediately; reappearance can acquire a new one. Non-simulator content without observers keeps its existing movement path.

Late points do not inherit the mode, attributes or finish action. Wreckage is not converted or withdrawn. A buggy defeated during the skill keeps its own recovery deadline; parent finish removes derived attributes without resetting that deadline or destroying the new wreckage. Both original effect packs contain **52 stretched-billboard renderers**. Their camera and velocity stretch scales are zero, freeform stretching is disabled, and rotation with stretch is enabled. ### Native Windows atomic-replacement checks (2026-10-15)

A continuously reopening reader can starve Windows file replacement. The atomic writer retains the old target and retries only Windows `EPERM`/`EACCES`/`EBUSY`, with thirty attempts, a 250 ms delay cap and 6.31 seconds of total scheduled wait. Other platforms and permanent error codes still fail immediately; exhausted retries leave the existing target intact. It never deletes the destination before replacement.

The concurrent-read consistency check yields briefly between complete reads. A separate Windows test holds a real .NET file handle without delete sharing until the parent releases it, beyond the former 1.27-second retry budget. It checks that the old JSON remains visible during the hold, replacement succeeds after release and no temporary files remain. This tests actual OS sharing behavior in addition to mocked retry/error paths.

Manual CI dispatch accepts `scope=atomic-json` for this targeted investigation. Its run and job names explicitly say Atomic JSON; it skips source-art preparation and the unrelated server smoke test. Default, push and PR runs still execute the full unit/integration suite and smoke test. A targeted green run is not a full-suite approval.

### Closure selected S3 and native slow_down clocks (2026-10-15)

The selected S3 command uses all ten original ranks, a thirty-second protected channel, eighteen one-DP pulses at the original 1.66-second interval and the -0.5 attack-time modifier. Native Begin/Loop/Idle clips cover all four facings; the loop releases at the literal 0.13333334028720856-second OnAttack event. Unlike ordinary/S2 windup selection, S3 selects at release. Each accepted attack counts once, independently of the number of projectiles, and every nine attacks adds one target to the next selection, up to seven. Vetoed casts and out-of-band forced attacks do not grow the counter. A new cast resets it.

Composite vision unions the owner main range, the command center's selected passive geometry and owned reinforcement main ranges. Active skill changes and movement refresh those main ranges, while extra composite keys are not recursively inherited. Reinforcement blockers remain selectable outside the composite. The command center retains passive geometry during recharge while its friend aura remains disabled; this is an explicit selected category/collider mapping, not recovered compiled dispatch. End/removal restores pre-existing extra range keys. Source aliasing, collider geometry and count/selection ordering remain stated local policies.

S3's original projectile is a target-following attachment with a 0.30000001192092896-second delay, rather than a speed-based traveling shot or zero-lifetime instant hit. The projectile system now supports that separate fixed-time attachment mode. The selected controller uses no placeholder traveling-arrow visual. Current owner ATK, the selected skill scale and the live owned-blocker trait determine normal physical damage at impact. Its non-missable slow_down parent is attached before missable damage; enemy-side tokens do not pass the native enemy-unit-type check. An emitted attachment can finish after owner withdrawal or skill end, but target death/disappearance/new-life and reentrant lifetime changes cancel it. Original native particles/audio are not supplied by this timing implementation.

`arkpedia-slow-down.js` separates native slow_down from movement-only Slow. Same-source applications stack and refresh to the selected rank's cap; different sources/names compete by current strength, with weaker fallback when the stronger source expires or is removed. The strongest live value applies one movement, ASPD and slow-down-clock multiplier, independently of other movement reductions. The native parent explicitly permits Resist; the existing application-time Resist normalization is retained. Its own eligible lifetime also follows the current slow-down multiplier.

Eligible buff durations consume slowed elapsed time while their periodic trigger frequency remains on world time. Named catalogue controls supply the existing AUTOMATIC eligibility mapping; original producers can explicitly mark eligibility or non-eligibility. Other native AUTOMATIC buff classification is not inferred. Enemy cooldown records can carry an explicit `affectedBySlowDown` flag, and a shared elapsed-time helper supports selected casting controllers. Unmarked enemy abilities keep their clock until original metadata is recovered; this implementation does not claim complete enemy cooldown, channel or animation coverage. ### Selective Stronghold enemy reuse (2026-10-16)

`content/enemies.js` now exposes `installSelected(battle, keys)` alongside its unchanged full-mode installation API. Both use the same existing factories and dispatch hooks. Selected requests copy and freeze an explicit set of known factories, install before the first enemy spawn, and are idempotent only for the same selection. Full and selected scopes cannot widen one another within a battle. Invalid or late selection fails before hook installation. This is a reuse mechanism, not public regular-stage approval.

`arkpedia-upstream-enemies.js` is the first held adapter. It requires an explicit contract and verifies its enemy data view and absence of seasonal overrides before selecting the inherited Wraith Leader kit. `review-upstream-enemies.mjs --fetch --check` verifies the complete frozen Global enemy-table Git blob, the original level-zero record and native prefab index before checking the receipt. The official description states that Wraith Leader cannot be blocked; it has no declared skills or talent blackboard and does not attack. The native index identifies its original hierarchy and absent attack/general/common ability clocks. It does not recover compiled class dispatch. The adapter maps the described permanent trait to Stronghold's existing unblockable spawn buff.

### Aphrissa public squad integration

Aphrissa (`char_4229_aphris`) and her passive relay (`token_10070_aphris_pc`) are now in the normal roster: 404/431 forms, 925 models, 27 forms remaining. All three source skills install the held S1/S2/S3 owners Codex reviewed (see docs/APHRISSA-REVIEW.md); there is no generic caster fallback. `data/arkpedia-aphrissa-runtime-review.json` gates admission the same way as the other recent operators. The build checks the source foundation, owner/relay art, relay portrait, interface pixels and clocks against their receipts, and the browser-review tooling against the recorded hashes.

The relay is an owner-controlled token, listed in `REGULAR_AUTOMATIC_TOKENS` so its model preloads with her. Its null skill slots come straight from the source table. Her original beam, hit and aura package is published as the second native effect package in `arkpedia-sd-assets` (`effects/native/aphrissa/…`, CN client `26-09-22-07-47-20_6c71fa`). The renderer loads it beside Tragodia's pass when she is in the squad and builds all 21 prepared roots at preload, so a broken input fails before battle. Beam end height (+0.65 above the end tile), hit height (+0.4) and identity orientation are explicit local mappings, not recovered native mount behaviour.

Reproduce:

```sh
node tools/arkpedia/export-aphrissa-delivery.mjs   # package for arkpedia-sd-assets' import-native-effect.mjs
node tools/arkpedia/build-mvp.mjs --sd-commit <published SD commit>
node --test test/arkpedia-aphrissa-*.test.js
ARKPEDIA_REVIEW_CHROME=/absolute/path/to/chromium ARKPEDIA_REVIEW_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:3182 node tools/arkpedia/review-aphrissa-public.mjs
```

`--review-candidate-aphrissa` builds the held candidate (with `ARKPEDIA_REVIEW_APHRISSA=1` for the tests) while the review receipt is pending. Native finish/FSM/control behaviour, audio, modules and compiled frame/pixel parity remain unapproved.

### Enemy records for every enemy (E1, 2026-10-21)

Enemies are moving to a data-driven, stage-agnostic model. The first step is one compiler for every Global enemy at every database level (`shared/arkpedia/enemy-records.js`).

- **What it reads.** The pinned `enemy_database` and `enemy_handbook_table`, plus a stage's `enemyDbRefs.overwrittenData`, applied the same way for any stage.
- **What a record keeps.** Stats, motion, attack mode, effective range (0 for melee), damage type, immunities, weight, life-point reduce, talents (grouped as `group.param`) and skills (prefab key, cooldowns, SP, blackboard).
- **Level rule.** Level 0 merged with the selected level, as the Stronghold builder does. The four database entries a cumulative merge would change are listed in the catalogue.
- **The catalogue.** `tools/arkpedia/enemy-records.mjs` writes `data/arkpedia-enemy-records.json`: 1,552 enemies, 1,736 level records, with the source commit and file hashes. `--check` regenerates it and compares.
- **The 0-1 build.** `build-mvp.mjs` now compiles the stage's enemies through the same compiler from the level file's `enemyDbRefs`, and refuses a geometry export that disagrees (Soldier's DEF 30 comes from the level file). Fields the old build dropped (range, damage type, immunities, talents, skills) are kept. Both 0-1 enemies stay stat-only, so behaviour is unchanged.
- **The harness.** `test/helpers/enemyHarness.js` `spawnAny(key, {level, stats, route, units, seconds})` spawns any enemy on the synthetic flat stage without a real stage.
- **Tests.** `test/arkpedia-enemy-records.test.js` covers the catalogue, the normalized definitions, the 0-1 records and a sweep that runs all 1,552 enemies for 12 s against a guard without engine errors. The full local suite passes 22,358 tests.

Behaviour support (the feature registry) and the support gate come next; `REGULAR_ENEMIES` still admits only the two 0-1 enemies.

### Derived enemy support and the stat-only tier (E2a, 2026-10-21)

`REGULAR_ENEMIES` is no longer a hand-written list; it is derived from the enemy catalogue and the native timing index.

- **Derivation.** `tools/arkpedia/enemy-support.mjs` (`shared/arkpedia/enemy-support.js`) writes `data/arkpedia-enemy-support.json` with every enemy's decision, and the compact registry `data/arkpedia-regular-enemies.json` that the battle and app load.
- **Rule.** An enemy is supported only when everything it uses has an approved implementation. Today that is the **stat-only tier**: no skills, no talents and no handbook abilities at any database level, and an original prefab with no native ability wrappers and no active general/common abilities. This is the same proof the Closure compatibility receipt used for the two 0-1 enemies.
- **Result.** 137 of 1,552 enemies are supported, including both 0-1 enemies. The other 1,415 list exactly what they are missing (`skill:<prefabKey>`, `talent:<group>`, `handbook-abilities`, `native-abilities:<prefab>`). The feature registry will clear those reasons batch by batch.
- **Tests.** `test/arkpedia-enemy-support.test.js` regenerates the support file from the committed inputs (so it also runs in CI). It checks that the registry equals the supported set and that every supported enemy uses nothing unimplemented, and fights each supported enemy against a guard on the harness stage until it dies or leaks. The full local suite passes 22,362 tests.

No stage spawns the newly supported enemies yet; stages stay test-only until the generic stage loader is reviewed.

### Enemy feature registry (E2b, 2026-10-21)

Behaviour attaches to enemies by feature, not by enemy id (`shared/arkpedia/enemy-features.js`).

- **What a feature is.** A handbook ability line (`ability:<text>`), a talent group (`talent:<group>`, with string-only parameters included) or a skill prefab key (`skill:<prefabKey>`).
- **What a registered feature declares.** `covers(record)`: the compiled record already models it, checked for every database level of every enemy that uses it. It may also declare a spawn `trait` that the battle applies (`installEnemyFeatures`, called by `StandardBattle` and the harness).
- **First approved features.**
  - Flying unit and Regenerates HP over time: already modelled by motion and `hpRecoveryPerSec`.
  - Cannot be blocked: an unblockable flag for life.
  - Invisible: the engine's enemy stealth, lifted by blocking for the STEALTH_RESTORE window.
  - Attacks two/2 targets simultaneously: two ranged targets per attack.
- **Coverage.** Support rises to 159 of 1,552 enemies: 137 stat-only, plus 22 through features. Wraith Leader is now admitted through "Cannot be blocked." rather than the held upstream kit, which stays unused.
- **Tests.** `test/arkpedia-enemy-features.test.js` checks each feature on every enemy it clears, through real harness behaviour (not blocked past a guard, stealth until blocked, regeneration, flying, two targets). The full local suite passes 22,443 tests.

### Enemy feature families, batch 1 (E3, 2026-10-21)

The feature runtime (`server/sim/content/arkpedia-enemy-features.js`) applies the declarative registry at spawn. It attaches abilities through a new features-only dispatch of `content/enemies.js` (`installFeatureDispatch`), reusing its documented ability builders (`featureAbilities`), never its per-enemy kits.

- **Talent families**, each keyed by its exact parameter signature:
  - Reborn/reborn (rebirth after the first knock-out);
  - periodic_damage (HP lost every second);
  - refracting (RES while not silenced);
  - atkup (ATK below half HP);
  - epdamage/EpDamage with `attack@ep_damage_ratio` (element damage on every hit; the element is the one term the handbook line names);
  - DeadSpawn (children on death).
- **Numbered ability lines**, matched by pattern and checked against the record:
  - "Must be damaged N times to defeat", and its Arts/True variant: a hit count equal to max HP;
  - "Can only be blocked by units with at least N Block": block weight.
- **Explained handbook lines.** A talent family declares the handbook lines it explains (for example "Will gradually lose HP over time"). A line with no feature of its own counts as covered only when a cleared talent of the same record explains it.
- **Spawn dependencies.** An enemy that spawns another is supported only when the child is too. `REGULAR_ENEMY_SPAWNS` makes a stage ship the children's records, and the harness supplies them.
- **Coverage.** Support rises to 207 of 1,552 enemies. Each family and pattern has a harness test on a real enemy.

### Retained native evidence and reviewed components (E4, 2026-10-21)

The native timing index is no longer the only retained evidence: `tools/arkpedia/extract-enemy-native-abilities.py` writes `data/arkpedia-enemy-native-abilities.json` with the original component JSON, object names, referenced components and buff templates that a reviewed feature reads. `shared/arkpedia/enemy-support.js` only accepts it when the source index hash and every component digest match (`verifiedNative`), so a changed prefab cannot silently keep an approval.

- **DefDown**: every attack hit adds one permanent, uncapped stack of `defdown.def` to the operator hit, proven against the original active-buff component (DEF addition, no duration, no stack cap).
- **Enhance**: each enemy-side death anywhere on the field grants one permanent stack of ATK and ASPD up to `enhance.max_stack_cnt`, proven against the original whole-field target validator and `ON_OWNER_KILLED` template.
- **Coverage.** Support rises to 231 of 1,552 enemies. The native-evidence hash checks are part of the support test.

### Death blasts, splits and the leak line (E5, 2026-10-21)

Three more regular-stage families attach through the same registry; no new per-enemy id list is involved.

- **`boom` death blast**: the reviewed handbook lines name Physical, Cold or Nervous-Impairment damage. `atk_scale` is the explosion multiplier, `freeze` the Cold duration and `ep_damage_ratio` the elemental rider. `deathBoom` now also applies the named element, and the battle selection rules stay the documented area/stealth/air rules.
- **`deathrattle` split**: "Splits into N <X> upon death" spawns `cnt` children after `delay` s on the parent's remaining route (`deathSpawnDelayed`), spread across the parent tile. The child is a normal spawn dependency, so the parent is supported only when the child is.
- **Leak line**: "Drains 1 Life Point when entering the Objective Point" only restates `lpr`, which the engine already applies on a leak.
- **Explained lines.** A feature may now explain a handbook line with a predicate as well as a regular expression, so variants such as "Death deals…" and "Deals … upon death" share one family.
- **Coverage.** Support rises to 243 of 1,552 enemies. The 12 new admits are both Infused Originium Slugs, both Infused Glacial Originium Slugs, both slug variants (their records use the same reviewed group and match the base slugs' stats), the Surprise Sponsor Drone, the neural 'Small Surprise' and the Originiutant split family. Tests exercise the physical, Cold and elemental blasts, the delayed split and the leak line on real enemies.

### Blocker ASPD and the tumor split (E6, 2026-10-21)

- **`atkSpeedDown`**: "When blocked, significantly reduces the blocker's ASPD" is a flat ASPD delta on the current blocker (the reviewed value is scaled by 100, matching the existing frost aura). The buff is owned by the enemy, moves with a new blocker and ends with its source.
- **Coverage.** Support rises to 246 of 1,552 enemies: the Originiutant Tumor and the two split variants that produce it. The test blocks a real tumor, checks the exact ASPD delta and verifies the debuff ends when the source dies.

### Stage catalogue (S1, 2026-10-21)

The client no longer hard-codes 0-1 as the only selectable stage.

- **Catalogue.** `data/arkpedia-stages.json` names the default and every stage: id, display code/name/description, and either an embedded stage (`data: null`, the current 0-1 slice) or a separate JSON file. The global 25 MB payload keeps the shared operator/enemy/effect data; a new stage should use the file-backed shape so it stays small.
- **Selection.** `shared/arkpedia/stages.js` validates the catalogue, resolves `?stage=` (defaulting to the catalogue default), fetches a file-backed stage, and installs it as `data.stage`. The battle and renderer still consume the same `data.stage` contract, so no stage consumer needs a branch.
- **UI.** The prep header and title read the installed stage, and a picker appears when the catalogue has more than one stage. An unknown `?stage=` lists the available stages instead of guessing.
- **Guardrails.** A file-backed stage must contain `geometry`; an embedded entry must match the global stage's code; every named data file must be committed. Tests cover default/explicit selection, the unknown-stage path, file replacement and the embedded mismatch.

### Sequential stage waves (S2, 2026-10-21)

`stageAdapter` no longer refuses a stage with more than one wave and no longer reads only `waves[0]`. It applies the public stage-playback rule: a wave's `pre_delay` is measured from the end of the previous wave, `duration + post_delay` advance the cursor, each spawn time is relative to its own wave, and `interval` spaces the count. Spawns are sorted by absolute time.

The fixed-squad guard was also ineffective: `suppliedUnits` is an object (`{fixed_squad, deployable_tokens}`), so the old `.length` check was always undefined. It now counts both lists, and the new test refuses a fixed squad, conditional spawns and an oversized grid. A second test pins the exact absolute times of a two-wave schedule.

### First file-backed stage data, 0-2 (S3, 2026-10-21, test-only)

`tools/arkpedia/build-stage.mjs` builds one stage file from the public stage/geometry sources and a stage-browser route export. It refuses a route export that does not match the geometry, runs the same `stageAdapter` and supported-enemy gate as 0-1, and records `art: null` / `gates: null` so the renderer falls back to its labelled simplified map.

`data/arkpedia-stage-0-2.json` is the first output: 6×10, three sequential waves, 14 spawns, the same two supported enemies as 0-1. It is **not in `data/arkpedia-stages.json`** yet: the owner's rule is that a new playable stage stays test-only until its simplified-art build and battle are reviewed. Tests pin its wave times and step a real `StandardBattle` through the first 30 seconds with no engine errors. When 0-2 is reviewed, adding it to the public simulator is one catalogue entry.

### Stage-owned enemy levels and overrides (S8, 2026-10-21)

A stage file must not reuse the database level-0 stats when its level file says otherwise. `build-stage.mjs` now reads each stage's `enemyConfigurations`:

- `database_level` selects the compiled catalogue level (4-1, 4-6 and 4-7 use level 1 for Soldier, Monster and the Caster variant).
- `overrides` applies the level file's owned attributes (`hp`, `atk`, `def`, `res`, `move_speed`, `attack_interval`, `attack_speed`, `weight`, `range`, `life_cost`, `taunt`, elemental resistances) to the record's stats. This restores, for example, 0-2/0-3's Soldier DEF 30 instead of the database's 100.

The generic stage test now asserts the level and every applied override, so a rebuilt stage cannot silently drift back to the database defaults. All 30 test-only files were regenerated with this rule.

### Cardinal splash and a DEF aura (E7, 2026-10-21)

- **Senior Caster**: its normal ranged attack also deals its normal damage type at ATK to the primary target's four cardinal neighbours (the target tile itself is excluded). The new `cardinalSplash` uses the shared area selection, so stealth/air/targetability rules stay the documented ones.
- **Defender-4**: "Increases the DEF of surrounding enemy units" is a silence-aware DEF aura within `defup.range_radius`, refreshed like the other enemy auras. The record's `defup.def` is the flat value.
- **Coverage.** Support rises to 250 of 1,552 enemies: Senior Caster, Shielded Senior Caster and Defender-4. The Senior Caster test places two adjacent guards and proves the second was hit by the splash; the Defender-4 test proves both nearby enemies gained the exact DEF.

### CI pushes stay off feature branches (S11, 2026-10-21)

The CI workflow now runs on `push` only to `master`; feature branches run when they have a pull request (plus `workflow_dispatch`). This removes the duplicate push+PR pair that previously started eight jobs per branch and left a cancelled duplicate check on the PR. The runner guard still enforces GitHub-hosted images for every job.

### Skullshatterer's grenade and the hp_ratio ATK buff (E8, 2026-10-21)

- **Grenade DEF-down**: the retained `skulsr_attack` native component is a one-stack, 5-second DEF multiplier (`defdown.def`, −0.5) on the target family. The reviewed branch applies it to the target and its four cardinal neighbours only while the caster is unblocked; the acid-slime branch keeps its permanent stacking flat DEF.
- **`atkup` with `hp_ratio`**: the low-HP ATK family now accepts both `['atk']` and `['atk','hp_ratio']`, reading the threshold from the record instead of assuming 50%.
- **Coverage.** Support rises to 251 of 1,552 enemies. The grenade test checks both adjacent guards, the exact DEF multiplier, and expiry five seconds after the source dies. 3-8 itself still cannot be built because its viewer export is missing route 0; the enemy is supported independently of that stage file.

### Developer QA view and the generated stage catalogue (S12, 2026-10-21)

`tools/arkpedia/stage-index.mjs` keeps `data/arkpedia-stages.json` in step with the stage files. Curated entries (the embedded 0-1, and any reviewed file-backed stage with no `testOnly`) are preserved; every other `data/arkpedia-stage-*.json` becomes a `testOnly` entry. `--check` fails when the catalogue is stale, and the stage-catalogue test runs the generator against the committed file.

`?experimental=1` opens the developer QA view: the stage picker lists all 58 entries (test-only ones marked “· test”), and an explicit test-only `?stage=` is accepted. Without the flag the public picker still shows only 0-1, and a test-only selection fails with a link to the QA view. The data and the loader remain the same; this is a review surface, not a public release. A headless Chrome pass opened 0-2 (three waves), 0-11, 3-1, 4-7 (stage-level enemy override), 5-8, 9-3 and S2-12 through the QA view: each rendered its code/name, the picker listed all 58 entries, and no page errors were reported.

### Claimed native wrappers and Crownslayer (E9, 2026-10-21)

The support gate can now distinguish an unreviewed native ability wrapper from one a feature has explicitly implemented. A feature may declare `nativeClaim(prefab, components)` returning the number of wrappers/active general-or-common abilities it covers; `enemySupport` subtracts those claims and records them as `claimedWrappers` / `claimedActive` in the native evidence. An unclaimed wrapper still refuses the enemy.

Crownslayer is the first user. The retained `Blink` pair is one EnemyAbility wrapper (familyMask 2, default init cooldown, no cast-like attack) plus its Blink ability (wait-for-attack event, no selector, one 1-second buff with abnormalFlags [3]). The `skill:blink` feature matches that exact shape, claims exactly one wrapper, and runs the reviewed `blinkForward` on the skill's 15-second cooldown when blocked. Silence stops it. Support rises to **252 of 1,552** enemies; the harness proves the blink fires and the wrapper claim is recorded.

### Unused viewer routes and the first boss stage (S13, 2026-10-21, test-only)

`stageAdapter` no longer demands a viewer path for a route that no wave spawns on. The stage browser legitimately omits an unused route, and the battle never walks it; a missing path for a used route is still refused. The new test pins both sides.

| 7-2 | 8×10 | 1 | 51 | its unused route 3 had no viewer path |

Coverage is **0-1 plus 60 test-only files** across Chapters 0–10 and S2.

### Reborn Creations (E10, 2026-10-21)

The Sarkaz Heirbearer family now has its reviewed creation mechanics:

- **`talent:dmg_res`**: the retained `damage_resistance` template is a Physical/Arts multiplier (`1 - dmg_res.damage_resistance`), applied with the persistent `enemy_bloodsucker_mark` identity buff from the active common ability.
- **`talent:buff_to_blocker`**: the current blocker gains `buff_to_blocker.block_cnt` Block (up to `max_valid_stack_cnt`) through the reviewed `enemy_bloodsucker_block_cnt[control]` template; each creation owns and removes its buff.
- **`talent:deathrattle`** now also covers "Will be reborn as … after falling in battle for the first time": one child after the review delay, with the same spawn dependency.
- **Native claim.** The active bloodsucker marker is claimed (`claimedActive: 1`) only when the complete `dmg_res` + block template + marker shape matches.

Support rises to **258 of 1,552** enemies. Tests cover the 90% reduction, the blocker's +1 Block, and the delayed reborn child.

### Viewer tunnels (S15, 2026-10-21, test-only)

A stage-browser route break is a tunnel, not a wall: the enemy disappears at the entrance point, waits the reviewed tunnel hold and appears at the first point after the break. `stageAdapter` now converts each break plus its matching `tunnel` hold into the engine's existing `DISAPPEAR` → `WAIT` → `APPEAR` legs instead of refusing the stage. A break without its hold, or a tunnel hold without its break, is still refused.

### Fixed-squad stages (S24, 2026-10-21, test-only)

The stage adapter now accepts a level file's `fixed_squad` (while still refusing `deployable_tokens`). The squad's `unit_id`, elite, level, potential, skill index and skill rank are compiled by `fixedSquadBuilds`; `StandardBattle` uses those builds instead of the caller's selection, and the prep page marks the squad as fixed. This is the squad the stage file owns, so the battle is reproducible and the UI no longer pretends a different selection matters.
